conviction_note: One counterparty fact leans positive: Allegion's Q3 on 22 Oct had Americas organic growth of +9.1%, non-residential up low double digits, and a raised guide. But ASSA has already risen 4.3% since 21 Oct, against an OMX down about 1.9%, so most of that read-across is in the price. ASSA gives no numeric guide, no Q3 consensus could be sourced, and Q2's 'beat' was partly one-offs. So p_up sits at 55 on a 5% move scale: +0.5 scaled, against an impact_sum of +0.4. Both are small and agree in sign.

Margin quality: unknown whether Q3 again carries tariff refunds, earnout reversals or divestment gains like Q2. Allegion booked $19.9m of IEEPA refunds in Q3, so ASSA may book more. A beat built on these is a sell risk.

findings.finding: Allegion, ASSA's closest US lock peer, reported Q3 2026 on 22 Oct: Americas revenue +9.1% organic, non-residential up low double digits on volume and price, International -0.2% organic, FY outlook raised. That is a direct counterparty read for ASSA's Americas division and the HID/Entrance US exposure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ASSA rose on organic and margin beats on its last prints: +5.9% (Jul 2025), +5.6% (21 Oct 2025, 'organic 3%, margin 16.9% vs 16.6% expected'), +4.9% (17 Jul 2026, organic 4% vs 2.7% expected). It fell 1.5% on 28 Apr 2026 (organic 2%).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. ASSA closed +2.33% on 22 Oct while the OMX fell 2.5%, and is +4.3% from 21 Oct to 26 Oct against an OMX down about 1.9%, so about 6 points of relative outperformance already sit in the price. What remains is that Allegion's Americas organic (+9.1%) ran well above ASSA's own Q2 Americas print (+4%); a matching acceleration at ASSA would be news. Allegion's flat International partly offsets this for ASSA's EMEIA, its biggest division. Sized net of that offset.
findings.independence: The same-day sector moves point the same way: Fortune Brands +6.9% and Kone +4.0% on 22 Oct (Yahoo daily bars, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/FBIN?range=1mo&interval=1d). That is a price reaction, not a second fundamental source.

findings.finding: ASSA's own Q2 presentation gives Q3 2026 run-rate effects on sales of FX 0% and M&A +2%, after -3% FX in Q2 and -6% in H1. So the currency drag that cost about 30-40bp of margin in Q2 should largely disappear in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No separate reaction to the FX line; it feeds headline EBIT, which the stock has rewarded when the margin beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the company guided it, and every analyst model carries the run-rate. It sits inside guidance, so sized near zero. Its only remaining value is that the Swedish report says the margin was 'negatively affected by currency effects and acquisition dilution, together 40 basis points', and that drag goes away.
findings.independence: Swedish Q2 report: 'Marginalen påverkades negativt av valutaeffekter och utspädning från förvärv, motsvarande sammanlagt 40 baspunkter' (https://www.assaabloy.com/group/sv/documents/investors/interim-reports/2026/Q2%20Kvartalsrapport%202026%20.pdf). Same issuer, so not independent.

findings.finding: Q2's record 17.0% EBIT margin, which the press reported as a beat against Factset's 6,370 MSEK, included divestment gains, earnout reversals and tariff refunds. The company's own underlying figure was 16.5%. So the headline Q3 y/y margin comparison is flattered or exposed depending on whether such items recur, and the H&M precedent says a refund-made beat gets sold.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 17 Jul 2026 the market looked through it: the stock rose 4.9% despite the one-offs in the headline beat. Allegion likewise rose 11% with $19.9m of IEEPA refunds in reported, though excluded from adjusted.
findings.original_quote: Justerat för reavinster vid avyttring, återföring av tilläggsköpeskillingar och återbetalningar av tullavgifter förbättrades den motsvarande rörelsemarginalen med 30 baspunkter jämfört med föregående år till 16,5% (16,2). [Adjusted for divestment gains, reversal of earnouts and tariff refunds, the corresponding operating margin improved by 30bp y/y to 16.5% (16.2).]
findings.why_not_priced: The Swedish wire copy reported Q2 as 'justerat rörelseresultat 6,680 vs 6,370 väntat', with no adjustment for the one-offs. If consensus extrapolated a 17%+ margin from that headline, a clean Q3 at about 16.8-17.0% reads as a miss on quality. Partly offset: the presentation footnote ('Including earnout reversals, divestment gain and tariff refund in Q2, 2026') was public and covering analysts read it. Small and of uncertain sign, so sized small.
findings.independence: Allegion's Q3 release shows IEEPA refunds still flowing in Q3 ($19.9m operating income), so ASSA may again carry refunds, which would cut against this finding (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001579241/000157924126000032/exhibit991-pressreleasedat.htm).

baseline_tension: The lean (-0.22, run-up only) is mildly negative and the 5-day run-up (+4.65%) is positive. My positive read-across agrees with the run-up, which is exactly why most of it is sized as already priced.
language_note: The Swedish Q2 report's CEO letter states the one-off composition plainly ('Justerat för reavinster vid avyttring, återföring av tilläggsköpeskillingar och återbetalningar av tullavgifter ... 16,5%'), while the Swedish wire copy (Finwire via Placera) headlined the unadjusted 6,680 vs 6,370 'beat'. The English presentation carries the same fact only as a footnote.

Placera/Finwire carried the 2025 and 2026 reaction context (+5.6% on Q3 2025, the Paclock bolt-on). Otherwise nothing the English sources did not already carry: every ASSA release is bilingual, and the decisive counterparty fact (Allegion) is English.
lessons_applied: 'Understatement is the systematic error' and 'too small about the move': abs_move_pct 4.5 -> 5.0, in line with ASSA's own actual-date reactions (5.9, 5.6, 4.9, 1.5) rather than the baseline's 2.53 cadence estimate
'A beat made of a one-off is sold' (H&M, tariff refund) supports keeping finding 3 negative; it was already sized with that in mind, so its size is unchanged and not applied twice
